Coordinator resource observation after Stage 1, not a device demonstration

The declared mode-alignment task only needs a one-particle selected-row bound. A balanced tree with32768leaves has15layers of disjoint two-mode combiners plus one parallel leaf-phase layer. In the one-particle space each layer is a direct sum. If each physical unitary block differs from its target by operator norm at most e, the entire layer differs by at most e, not by its number of blocks. Telescoping16unitary layers gives ||U_actual-U_target||<=16e, hence selected-row error<=16e.

Under exactly these independent-local-unitary/no-extra-mode assumptions, the Stage 1 remaining row budget.020028 allows e<=.00125175. Its sum-over-all65535elements bound3.0562e-7 is sufficient but very conservative. Each optical element's multiple control angles may contribute more than one local-error term; include those constants. Disjointness/correct wiring and uniform block-error guarantees must be real. Generic added noise, crosstalk, asynchronous/mode mismatch, differing loss and dephasing are not covered by a unitary-layer bound. The full Fock-unitary norm need not obey this dimension-free bound; the conclusion is the ONE-PARTICLE mode row, precisely the receiver's alignment contract.

This changes neither the32767combiner count nor the required parallel hardware, cold ports, total sampling or loss depth. It is not a practical superiority claim. It is an example of the relevant quantity admitting a cheaper certificate than a global worst-case implementation bound. Stage2already has freedom to replace these sufficient constants; no supplemental active-parent message has been sent. Revisit if its next construction is limited by the old precision number.
